title: Theorem on formal functions at a point of the base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism] with $Y$ locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent] and let $y\in Y$, with local ring $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ (a Noetherian local ring) and maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_y$. For $n\ge1$ let $c_n:\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n)\to Y$ be the canonical morphism (induced by $\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n$), $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n)\times_YX$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] (the $n$th infinitesimal neighbourhood of the fibre $X_1=X_y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]), $i_n:X_n\to X$ the projection and $\mathcal F_n=i_n^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; the closed immersions $j_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ (base change of $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n)\to\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^{n+1})$, with $i_{n+1}\circ j_n=i_n$) induce maps $H^p(X_{n+1},\mathcal F_{n+1})\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] (pullback along $j_n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] followed by the canonical isomorphism $j_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$), each $H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ being an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_y^n$-module. Fix $p\ge0$ and let $M=(R^pf_*\mathcal F)_y$ be the stalk at $y$ of the higher direct image [pqf-def-cohomology], an $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-module, and $M^\wedge=\varprojlim_nM/\mathfrak m_y^nM$ its $\mathfrak m_y$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Since $R^pf_*\mathcal F$ is the sheaf associated with $V\mapsto H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf], $M=\varinjlim_{V\ni y}H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$; as $X_n\to X$ factors through $f^{-1}(V)$ for every open $V\ni y$, pulling back along $X_n\to f^{-1}(V)$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] defines $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-linear maps $\theta_n:M\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$, compatible with the transition maps and vanishing on $\mathfrak m_y^nM$. Then the induced map $\theta:M^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$-modules (indeed of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}^\wedge$-modules), and its composite with $M\to M^\wedge$ is $(\theta_n)_n$. In particular ($p=0$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, so $\mathcal F_n=\mathcal O_{X_n}$) $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y^\wedge\cong\varprojlim_nH^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ via the maps $(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y\to H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ sending the germ of $t\in\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}(V))$ to its pullback to $X_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma Tag 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, line 5721) and its proof (flat base change to Spec O_{Y,y}, Lemma 02KH lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology, then Theorem 02OC theorem-formal-functions); the description of the maps theta_n is the one in the proof of Tag 0G7X (perfect.tex, lines 8130-8157), which uses that M^ -> H^0(X_1) is the canonical map

proof.text: (The local ring and the canonical morphism.) Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_y$. As $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $y$ lies in an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $R$ Noetherian, and $A\cong R_{\mathfrak p}$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]; so $Y'=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $c:Y'\to Y$ be the canonical morphism and $y'$ the closed point of $Y'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism]: $c$ is flat, $c(y')=y$, $c^{-1}(V)=Y'$ for every open $V\ni y$, the stalk map $\mathcal G_y\to(c^*\mathcal G)_{y'}$ is an isomorphism for every $\mathcal O_Y$-module $\mathcal G$, and $c_n=c\circ c'_n$ with $c'_n:\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)\to Y'$ the closed immersion given by the quotient map (part (5) with $J=\mathfrak m^n$). This is 'c is a flat morphism as it identifies local rings' and the hint 'the morphisms $c_n$ factor through $c$' of the source.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (The base change.) Let $X'=Y'\times_YX$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$, and $\mathcal F'=g'^*\mathcal F$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Then $f'$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b), hence of finite type, so $X'$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] (Step 1). $\mathcal F$ is coherent on the locally Noetherian $X$ ([pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] for $f$), hence quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; so $\mathcal F'$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent] and of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-support-pullback-finite-type] (3), hence coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. Also $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (finite type and separated, [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Since $c(Y')\subseteq V$ for every open $V\ni y$ (Step 1), $g'(X')\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ and $f'^{-1}(c^{-1}V)=X'$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (The stalk is $H^p(X',\mathcal F')$.) Define $\varphi:M\to H:=H^p(X',\mathcal F')$ by $\varphi([\xi]_V)=(g'_V)^*\xi$ for $\xi\in H^p(f^{-1}(V),\mathcal F)$, where $g'_V:X'\to f^{-1}(V)$ is $g'$ (Step 2) and $(g'_V)^*$ the pullback [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) (with $(g'_V)^*(\mathcal F|_{f^{-1}V})=\mathcal F'$); it is well defined because pullback commutes with restriction to smaller $V$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2),(3), and $A$-linear, $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ acting on $H$ through $A=\Gamma(Y',\mathcal O_{Y'})\to\Gamma(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ (linearity in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], $c^\sharp$ inducing the identity of $A$ on stalks, Step 1). $\varphi$ is bijective: let $G=R^pf_*\mathcal F$ and $G'=R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$. By flat base change [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] ($c$ flat, $f$ qcqs, $\mathcal F$ quasi-coherent) the base change map $\beta:c^*G\to G'$ is an isomorphism ($g'$ is flat as a base change of $c$, so the base change map of Stacks 02N7 is defined). By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-map-sections] its adjoint $\beta^\flat=c_*(\beta)\circ\eta_G:G\to c_*G'$ sends $[\xi]_V$ to the class of $(g'_V)^*\xi$ in $G'(c^{-1}V)=G'(Y')$. Take stalks: the composite $G_y\to(c^*G)_{y'}\xrightarrow{\beta_{y'}}G'_{y'}$, whose first arrow is the isomorphism of Step 1 (germ of the unit $\eta_G$), sends $[\xi]_V$ to the germ at $y'$ of the class of $(g'_V)^*\xi$, so it is an isomorphism. Finally $G_y=M$ and $G'_{y'}=\varinjlim_{W\ni y'}H^p(f'^{-1}W,\mathcal F')=H^p(X',\mathcal F')$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf], [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], since $Y'$ is the only open of $Y'$ containing the closed point $y'$ of the local scheme (an open containing $\mathfrak m$ contains every prime of $A$, all being generalizations of $\mathfrak m$). Under these identifications the composite is $\varphi$; hence $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules (Stacks: $c^*R^pf_*\mathcal F=R^pf'_*\mathcal F'$ by 02KH, and $(R^pf'_*\mathcal F')_{y'}=\Gamma(Y',R^pf'_*\mathcal F')=H^p(X',\mathcal F')$; the stalk route used here avoids the affine-base lemma 01XK). (Linearity and the degree-0 description of these maps: [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties].)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800); Lemma 02KH (lemma-flat-base-change-cohomology) and Cohomology Lemma 02N7 (base change map)

proof.text: (The infinitesimal neighbourhoods are identified.) Let $p_n:X_n\to\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)$ be the second projection. Since $f\circ i_n=c_n\circ p_n=c\circ c'_n\circ p_n$ (Step 1), the universal property of $X'$ [def-pc-fibre-product] gives a unique $i'_n:X_n\to X'$ with $g'\circ i'_n=i_n$ and $f'\circ i'_n=c'_n\circ p_n$, and $(X_n,i'_n,p_n)$ is a fibre product $X'\times_{Y'}\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^n)$ (pasting of the two cartesian squares, by the universal properties). Hence by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (1),(2) for $f'$ and $K=\mathfrak m^n$, $i'_n$ is a closed immersion with ideal sheaf $\mathfrak m^n\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal I^n$, $\mathcal I=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X'}$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $i'_n$ is affine (preimages of affine opens are affine) [pqf-def-affine-morphism]; by its part (3) the transition closed immersion $j_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ satisfies $i'_{n+1}\circ j_n=i'_n$ (uniqueness in the universal property of $X'$, as $g'i'_{n+1}j_n=i_{n+1}j_n=i_n$). Moreover $\mathcal F_n=i_n^*\mathcal F=(g'\circ i'_n)^*\mathcal F\cong i'^*_n\mathcal F'$ canonically [def-pc-module-pullback], and $\mathcal F_n$ is quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. ('The infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the fibre $X_y$ and $X'_y$ are identified (verification omitted)' in the source.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (The maps $\theta_n$ factor through $\varphi$.) Let $u_n:\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ be the $i'_n$-map adjoint to the isomorphism $i'^*_n\mathcal F'\cong\mathcal F_n$ (the unit $\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}i'^*_n\mathcal F'$ followed by it), and $\theta'_n=u_n^*:H\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$, i.e. the pullback along $i'_n$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. By definition $\theta_n([\xi]_V)$ is the pullback of $\xi$ along $i_n:X_n\to f^{-1}(V)$, which is $i_n=g'_V\circ i'_n$; by [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2) (and the compatibility of the canonical isomorphisms $(g'i'_n)^*\cong i'^*_ng'^*$ with the units [def-pc-module-pullback]) $\theta_n=\theta'_n\circ\varphi$. Likewise $i'_n=i'_{n+1}\circ j_n$ gives $\tau_n\circ\theta'_{n+1}=\theta'_n$ for the transition maps $\tau_n:H^p(X_{n+1},\mathcal F_{n+1})\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ of the statement, so the $\theta_n$ are compatible with the transition maps. All these maps are $A$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], and $A$ acts on $H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ through $A\to\Gamma(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$, which factors through $A/\mathfrak m^n$ ($f'\circ i'_n=c'_n\circ p_n$); hence $\theta_n$ vanishes on $\mathfrak m^nM$ and $\theta'_n$ on $\mathfrak m^nH$. (Linearity and the degree-0 description of these maps: [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties].)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (Cohomology of $X_n$ as cohomology on $X'$.) Let $q_n:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'$ be the quotient map (notation of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0)). Since $i'_n$ is a closed immersion with ideal $\mathcal I^n$ (Step 4), the unit $\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}i'^*_n\mathcal F'$ is surjective with kernel $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-unit-quotient]; composing with $i'_{n*}$ of $i'^*_n\mathcal F'\cong\mathcal F_n$ gives an isomorphism $\rho_n:\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ with $\rho_n\circ q_n=u_n$ ('$i_{n,*}\mathcal F_n=i_{n,*}i_n^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F/\mathfrak m^n\mathcal F$' in the source). As $i'_n$ is affine and $\mathcal F_n$ quasi-coherent (Step 4), the edge map $e_n:H^p(X',i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n)\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] ('by the Leray spectral sequence for $i_n$' in the source). Put $\psi_n=e_n\circ H^p(\rho_n):H^p(X',\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F')\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2), $\psi_n=\rho_n^*$ is the map of the $i'_n$-map $\rho_n$ and $\psi_n\circ H^p(q_n)=(\rho_n\circ q_n)^*=u_n^*=\theta'_n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800); Cohomology of Schemes Lemma 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology) for the Leray step

proof.text: (The $\psi_n$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems.) Let $\pi_n:\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'$ be the transition map ($\pi_n\circ q_{n+1}=q_n$) and $t_n:\mathcal F_{n+1}\to j_{n*}\mathcal F_n$ the $j_n$-map defining $\tau_n=t_n^*$ (Step 5). By [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-functorial] (2), $\tau_n\circ\psi_{n+1}$ is the map of the $i'_n$-map $a=i'_{n+1,*}(t_n)\circ\rho_{n+1}$ and $\psi_n\circ H^p(\pi_n)$ that of $b=\rho_n\circ\pi_n$, both morphisms $\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^{n+1}\mathcal F'\to i'_{n*}\mathcal F_n$. Now $b\circ q_{n+1}=\rho_n\circ q_n=u_n$, and $a\circ q_{n+1}=i'_{n+1,*}(t_n)\circ u_{n+1}$, which is the $i'_n$-map adjoint to the composite of the canonical isomorphisms $i'^*_n\mathcal F'\cong j_n^*i'^*_{n+1}\mathcal F'\cong j_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\cong\mathcal F_n$, i.e. again $u_n$ (the canonical isomorphisms of iterated pullbacks are compatible [def-pc-module-pullback]). Since $q_{n+1}$ is an epimorphism, $a=b$, so $\tau_n\circ\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ H^p(\pi_n)$: $(\psi_n)_n$ is an isomorphism of inverse systems from $(H^p(X',\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F'))_n$ to $(H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n))_n$, and $\varprojlim\psi_n$ is an isomorphism. (This is the compatibility the source leaves implicit in 'hence we may indeed apply the theorem on formal functions to compute the limit'.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800)

proof.text: (Theorem on formal functions over $A$.) $A$ is Noetherian, $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ proper and $\mathcal F'$ coherent (Steps 1-2), and $\mathcal I=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X'}$ with $\mathcal I^n=\mathfrak m^n\mathcal O_{X'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-base-change-closed-immersion-ideal] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-theorem-formal-functions] (with $I=\mathfrak m$), the maps $H/\mathfrak m^nH\to H^p(X',\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F')$ induced by $H^p(q_n)$ give an isomorphism $H^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X',\mathcal F'/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F')$. Composing with $\varprojlim\psi_n$ (Step 7) and using $\psi_n\circ H^p(q_n)=\theta'_n$ (Step 6): the map $\theta':H^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ induced by the $\theta'_n$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 02OD (lemma-formal-functions-stalk, lines 5759-5800); Theorem 02OC (theorem-formal-functions)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The $A$-isomorphism $\varphi:M\to H$ (Step 3) induces isomorphisms $M/\mathfrak m^nM\to H/\mathfrak m^nH$ and so an isomorphism of completions $\varphi^\wedge:M^\wedge\to H^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. By Step 5, $\theta_n=\theta'_n\circ\varphi$, so the map $\theta:M^\wedge\to\varprojlim_nH^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ induced by the $\theta_n$ equals $\theta'\circ\varphi^\wedge$ (Step 8), an isomorphism, and $\theta\circ(M\to M^\wedge)=(\theta_n)_n$ by construction. $\theta$ is $A^\wedge$-linear: $A^\wedge=\varprojlim A/\mathfrak m^n$ acts componentwise on $M^\wedge$ and on $\varprojlim_nH^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ (each $H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$ being an $A/\mathfrak m^n$-module, Step 5), and $\theta$ is componentwise the $A/\mathfrak m^n$-linear map $M/\mathfrak m^nM\to H^p(X_n,\mathcal F_n)$. For $p=0$, $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$: $\mathcal F_n=i_n^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X_n}$, $M=(f_*\mathcal O_X)_y$ [lem-weil-pbc-higher-direct-image-presheaf], and in degree $0$ the pullback sends a section $t\in\mathcal O_X(f^{-1}V)$ to its pullback $i_n^\sharp(t)\in H^0(X_n,\mathcal O_{X_n})$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], which is the special case stated. (Linearity and the degree-0 description of these maps: [lem-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap-basic-properties].)
